A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same complete, readable ten-page paper, including all figures, tables, references, and Appendices A–D. Text and rendered-page comparisons establish that only the first-page arXiv version/date stamp differs.

before.justification: Section 4 reports original Llama-2-7B experiments comparing LIMA and Alpaca-Longest across training settings. Appendix A reports corresponding Mistral results, supported by Figures 1–2 and Tables 2–3.

after.justification: v3 retains the original Llama-2-7B and Mistral experiments and their reported win/tie counts in Section 4 and Appendix A.

M1.justification: Both retain the same instruction-tuning procedures and model-based assessment of data quality. No architecture, training objective, algorithmic component, or inference procedure is revised.

E1.justification: Both use LIMA and Alpaca-Longest for training and Koala, MT-Bench, and Self-Instruct for evaluation. No dataset, task, domain, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: The LIMA-versus-Alpaca-Longest comparisons and comparisons against Setting 1 are identical in Figures 1–2 and Tables 2–3. No evaluated comparator changes.

E3.justification: The same 16 hyperparameter configurations, Llama-2-7B and Mistral-7B-v0.3 models, sample sizes, and GPT-4o judging protocol are retained. Settings in Section 3 and Appendices C–D are identical.

E4.justification: The hyperparameter sensitivity analyses, within-dataset comparisons across settings, Mistral analyses, and GPT-4o/GPT-4o-mini agreement analysis are unchanged in Section 4 and Appendices A and D.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting is identical. Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests; the correlation analysis in Appendix D is retained unchanged.

E6.justification: All numerical results and reported trends in Figures 1–2 and Tables 2–3 match. Appendix D also retains the same judge correlation of 0.559 and reported evaluation costs.

T1.justification: Neither version presents formal theorems, proofs, or mathematical derivations. The conceptual reasoning about data quality and locally optimal training settings is identical.

C1.justification: Both claim that arbitrary hyperparameter choices can reverse data-quality conclusions and advocate justified, locally optimal settings. The abstract, introduction, and conclusion are unchanged.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning undertraining, model-based assessment, and hyperparameter-search costs are identical. Qualifications about untested hyperparameters, optimization scope, and judge choice remain unchanged, including the limitations and appendices.

D1.justification: Appendices C–D retain identical hardware, software, sequence-length, gradient-accumulation, judge-prompt, and decoding details. No implementation or resource-access disclosure changes.

R1.justification: Section 2, the literature survey in Table 1, and the reference list are identical. Positioning relative to prior LIMA, Alpaca-Longest, and hyperparameter research is unchanged.

P1.justification: The first-page arXiv stamp changes from v1, 4 Mar 2025 to v3, 16 May 2025. The title, authors, prose, terminology, section order, and appendix structure are otherwise identical.

P2.justification: Figures 1–2, Tables 1–5, captions, placement, and page layout are unchanged. Pages 2–10 render identically; the first-page difference is confined to version/date stamp text.

improvement.justification: The complete comparison, including Appendices A–D, establishes unchanged scientific content, empirical evidence, reasoning, reproducibility details, and layout. Updating the arXiv version/date stamp produces no meaningful gain or loss in overall paper quality.
